dialogue.title: Fort Solid at night
paragraphs: The fort's curfew escorts you away; it does not order Soldiers or Captain Eir to attack you. See Eir's nighttime rules for the hours, perimeter and story permissions. Attacking friendly characters can still cause retaliation; see Aggression rules.

classifications.note: Character/NPC presentation grouping; this does not assert peaceful behavior.

dialogue.title: Information
paragraphs: Eir explains that newcomers may visit Magus Clay in the undercroft during the day, but must leave the fort's perimeter at night. Clay buys and sells supplies there. Her Information option disappears once she grants access to the commander.

dialogue.title: Advice
paragraphs: Early on, Eir suggests visiting the two other Unwanted at the camp marked on your starting map. This is the lead into the camp investigation, not a repeatable errand.
After you hand over the Wooden Recorder, choosing Advice goes straight to her survival tips instead. Before that, More Advice follows the camp suggestion.

dialogue.title: More Advice
paragraphs: Eir recommends preparing above ground before exploring caves: collect larger branches from dead trees during daylight, look for Flint among rocks, and build a Campfire before a cold night.

This is preparation advice, not a cave-entry requirement. Tree harvesting and Ground debris explain the material sources. A campfire needs fuel and a separate ignition attempt; Temperature explains warmth, wet clothing and exposure.

dialogue.title: Fort Solid at night
paragraphs: The curfew causes an escort-out scene, not a night-only attack by Soldiers or Eir. It checks after a turn advances the clock, from 21:00 through 05:00 inclusive. At exactly 05:00 it still applies; after 05:00 and before 21:00 it does not. These are fixed hours, not the lighting system's dusk or dawn.

Until you earn permission to remain, the outdoor check covers a 10-tile radius around the fort's reference point, not its entire world-map zone. Inside Clay's undercroft, the early-game check applies throughout that interior. A fade moves you out rather than starting a guard fight; the outdoor escort also advances another turn.

The escort check does not require a nearby Soldier or Eir, and is skipped while a screen transition is already running. Their normal friendly targeting and retaliation rules are separate; see Aggression rules.

dialogue.title: Earning nighttime access
paragraphs: The undercroft exemption begins when you deliver the three rift samples to Clay. You may then remain inside at night, although the outdoor perimeter restriction still applies. Continue his conversation for permission to use his storage chest and alchemy station.

The remaining curfew ends after you bring Viend back and speak with Eir. Her invitation to meet Commander Tain grants fort access and removes the outdoor escort restriction. Simply delivering the Wooden Recorder or reaching the next midnight does not lift it.

dialogue.title: Quest guidance
paragraphs: The camp lead continues by taking the Wooden Recorder to Eir. Wait for the next midnight, then speak with her again to be sent to Clay. Returning immediately at midnight can still trigger the curfew; the quest timer and nighttime access are different rules.
Once Clay has the rift samples, Eir supplies the direction to Ranger Bhato. Follow the journal's direction for your world and Bhato's location instructions.

dialogue.title: Advice
paragraphs: Clay recommends searching beneath rocks and boulders for useful finds, including small animals, and examining creatures before fighting them.

Ground debris and Searching boulders list the possible finds and their conditions; a search does not guarantee every item he mentions. Use Examine to inspect a creature rather than guessing its capabilities. The Bestiary, Health and armor and Damage types pages explain the combat information.

dialogue.title: Undercroft at night
paragraphs: Early visits to the undercroft are subject to Eir's nighttime rules. The undercroft earns its own exemption before the rest of the fort; see nighttime access for the quest requirements.

dialogue.title: Quest guidance
paragraphs: After Eir sends you to him, Clay requests three rift samples. Handing them over advances his research; continue talking to obtain access to the storage chest and Alchemy workstation, then return to Eir.

Later, bring Bhato's rune to Clay. He provides Clay's Strange Potion for the return to the dead camp. His subsequent instructions send you to investigate ruins and warn about the toadkin around them. Follow the journal's old-records objective rather than treating his ordinary Advice option as another quest.

dialogue.title: Advice
paragraphs: Bhato recommends retreating from an area that is too difficult and returning after improving your skills and supplies. This is general survival guidance, not a level requirement imposed by the conversation. Level progression explains advancement; Resting explains recovery before another expedition.

dialogue.title: Quest guidance
paragraphs: When Eir sends you to Bhato, he describes a poisonous Sceetler that fled into an ancient cellar and gives you two Minor Antidotes. Follow the cellar objective, not the entrance to his hut. Poison explains the damage and remedies.
Recover the creature's rune and report back to Bhato. His reward conversation unlocks his storage chest and Workstation and sends you to Clay with the rune.
Bhato's hideout is in a Common Bog directly north, south, east or west of Fort Solid, never diagonally. Its zone is chosen at world creation.

Neighboring zones are checked north, south, east for a column A fort, or west, north, south for a column E fort. At most one becomes Vast Waters; the rest become Common Bogs. Bhato takes the last Common Bog in that order, so directions are not equally likely.
Captain Eir gives the direction, which is recorded in your journal. Look for a small foliage-roof hut, placed when you first enter its zone. Enter the hut, not the nearby ancient cellar.

dialogue.title: Information
paragraphs: Viend says he formerly practiced healing magic and was exiled for helping people the Kingdom rejected. Continue the conversation to hear why he dislikes the magi's practice of treating everyone else as inferior.
These two Information responses describe his background; they are not a request to collect items. His later trading access is separate from this conversation.

dialogue.title: Quest guidance
paragraphs: After his revival, Viend asks you to escort him to Fort Solid because Eir still believes him dead. Follow Escort Viend and then A successful return. Talking to Eir afterward is also the step that earns full nighttime access.

ability.title: Healing
paragraphs: Viend automatically heals up to two ordinary wounds on one character within 16 tiles. Each cast restores 1 HP to each of two randomly chosen wounded health cells, or just 1 HP if only one cell is wounded. It costs him 10 action points, his full turn's allowance, and has no separate cooldown.

The player always takes priority, even if someone else is closer or more badly injured. Otherwise, Viend heals himself if wounded, then the nearest eligible friendly character. He does not heal dead or incapacitated NPCs. Walls and other obstacles do not block the spell.

Healing restores HP, not armor or wellbeing, and does not remove poison, bleeding or sickness. Burns cannot be healed directly: use Simple Burn Remedy to turn them into ordinary wounds first. See Resting for natural wound healing.

Viend checks for wounds before moving or attacking whenever he can act with all 10 action points available. Ongoing damage or a stun can delay or prevent his action. Healing needs no conversation, payment or supplies, works outside combat, and does not depend on his shop or alchemy workstation.

During his escort or an active summon, Viend receives an action each turn. When nearby but idle, neither fighting nor detecting an enemy, he normally has a 10% chance to act each turn, so healing can be intermittent. While you rest in a bed or sleeping gear, this idle chance falls to 1.5% if at least two conditions are met: satiation above its low threshold, stamina above its low threshold, and temperature inside its comfortable range.

dialogue.title: Trade
paragraphs: Tain directs ordinary supply requests to Magus Clay and offers map ledgers himself. His ordinary menu has Trade, not a separate Information or Advice option; his expedition guidance occurs during the main quest.

dialogue.title: Quest guidance
paragraphs: Tain points you toward the ancient-city expedition and recommends training and preparing before departure. Speak to Clay first: Prepare for the journey leads into the old-records search. The location he names is taken from your world's Library coordinates, not a fixed map square.
Continuing his briefing grants one Summoning Stone for calling an ally. This is a story reward, not a purchase from his map stock.

dialogue.title: Information
paragraphs: Gurb-Gurb identifies himself as toadkin, but says his unusual awareness and ability to converse set him apart. He cannot clearly remember how this change happened. This is his personal account, not an explanation of a player transformation mechanic or a quest objective.

dialogue.title: Field-kit tip during Trade
paragraphs: Gurb-Gurb's practical tip is in Trade: a Survivor's Field Kit is useful away from permanent workstations, but you must supply its fire yourself.

The kit's crafting menu is available only while its fire is active. See Survivor's Field Kit for recipes and Campfire for the separate fuel and lighting requirements; owning the kit alone does not make those recipes usable.

Gurb-Gurb's hollow is placed when you first enter a Drowned Fen while it remains uncreated. Revisits and loading an outdoor save also trigger the check; caves do not. A Savage Mirk is eligible only in a world with no Drowned Fen. Normal new worlds always have one.
When the hollow appears, a smoke-discovery message and five white dots point toward it. This one-time cue shows direction, not a safe path. Smoke rises from the hollow during play.
Gurb-Gurb is inside the hollow tree stump.

dialogue.title: Information
paragraphs: Ihar says he fled to the Mirk while still wanted by the Kingdom, rather than being sentenced to exile as an Unwanted. Continue to hear about his failed rebellion and his doubts about his own ambitions.
This is character history, not a rebellion quest or a requirement for buying his goods.

dialogue.title: Trade
paragraphs: Ihar explains that he claimed the shipwreck and its cargo of military equipment after losing his own boat. This supplies the background to his shop, not a separate treasure-recovery objective. His wares are listed below.

Ihar lives in a wooden shipwreck on a Broken Fen shoreline. Entering a Broken Fen attempts to place it if it has not appeared yet. A search can fail after 1280 attempts to find suitable sand and water, even when a valid spot exists.

After a failed search, enter the same or another Broken Fen to retry. Revisits and loading an outdoor save count; caves do not. There is no alternative-biome fallback. Normal new worlds have Broken Fens; a world without them cannot place this wreck.
Once placed, the wreck stays in that location. Ihar is inside.

NPC placement remains an editorial inference: the inspected creation, dialogue and merchant routes do not establish an ordinary encounter or story role. Generic retaliation is distinct from normal target acquisition.

A skill at rank ten cannot rise further and does not consume the point.
entry_display.summary: Each of the five groups has five skills, starting at rank zero and capped at rank ten.

steps: Update the rain-history balance by adding 1/180 while rain power is positive or subtracting 1/360 otherwise, then clamp the balance between minus one and one.
Clear weather tests a cloud threshold of the larger of 2% and 12% times one minus the balance.
Cloudy weather first tests clearing: the larger of 2% and 10% times one plus the balance. Only after failure does it test rain: the larger of 2% and 30% times one minus the balance.
The early-game protection described above can block this transition from clouds to new rain; it does not promise clear skies throughout the protected period.

Rainy weather first tests return to clouds using the larger of 1% and 25% times one plus the balance. Only after failure does it test direct clearing using the larger of 1% and 5% times one plus the balance.
If rain continues, intensity changes by a random amount between minus 10 and plus 10 percentage points and is clamped to its limits. Ending rain can fade over subsequent turns.
entry_display.summary: Weather checks run on hourly turn boundaries. Later checks run only if earlier ones fail.

entry_display.title: Exploration order
entry_display.summary: New terrain blends into neighboring zones you have already explored.
steps: Entering an unsaved zone creates fresh terrain. Saved zones load their existing terrain instead.
Gurb-Gurb and Ihar can still appear on first visits, revisits or outdoor save loads until their locations have been created. See their pages for biome and placement rules.
Quantity rolls mix increasingly wide inclusive integer ranges, favoring lower counts.
Treasure candidates must meet budget, minimum-value, type, size and story requirements.
Accepted items spend the remaining budget. Generation stops at 500 counted candidates; undefined items and the early Summoning Stone story exclusion do not count.
Durability and stack size can vary. Independent bonus checks can succeed together.
entry_display.title: Quantities and treasure budgets
entry_display.summary: Low quantities are more common than high ones. Treasure uses a value budget rather than equal per-item odds.

steps: The treasure budget is 1 silver, with a minimum non-valuable item value of 10 copper. Coins and gems bypass that minimum but must fit the budget.
Food and materials can appear, unlike ordinary skeleton treasure. Other exclusions, story requirements, wear and selection limits still apply.
Recovered arrows are added after the base loot.
entry_display.summary: Raving Unwanted and Mutated Unwanted have random treasure rather than fixed loot. Lootable corpses can also contain recovered arrows.
entry_display.conditions: Only arrows retained by the recovery check are added; not every fired arrow is recoverable.

entry_display.title: Using crafting methods
entry_display.summary: Different crafting methods offer different recipes.
steps: Some components are required as tools rather than consumed ingredients.
Where chopping is required, a carried tool must meet the recipe's chopping-capability requirement.

entry_display.summary: Temperature has seven named bands. Values above 0.85 are Blazing hot.
steps: Check thresholds from lowest to highest, including equality.
Use the first matching label.
Clothing, wetness, shade and warmth-loss modifiers affect temperature separately.

entry_display.summary: XP thresholds grow exponentially and round down to a multiple of five. Excess XP carries over; each update awards at most one level.
steps: For current level L, multiply 28 by 1.2 raised to L, then round down to a multiple of five.
Compare rounded XP with the threshold. On leveling up, subtract the threshold and keep the remainder.
Gain one skill point per level and one HP allocation point every third level.
At the level cap, XP stays below the next threshold.

stations.title: Inventory crafting
stations.summary: Craft directly from the inventory crafting menu.

stations.title: Campfire
stations.summary: Use a lit campfire for its cooking options.
notes: Lighting a fire is a separate one-AP attempt that also requires fuel and a successful ignition check.
Fire-linked crafting is available only while the fire remains active; its recipe menu closes when the fire goes out.

stations.title: Survivor's Field Kit
stations.summary: A portable alternative to the alchemy workstation with the same 15 recipes. It requires an active fire; fuel and access requirements differ from the permanent workstation.

stations.title: Chopping Log
notes: The Chopping Log halves the base AP cost of firewood recipes.

stations.title: Primitive Farmwork Table
stations.summary: A workstation for the farmwork recipes listed below.

stations.title: Alchemy workstation
stations.summary: Both alchemy workstations offer the same recipes without an active fire.
notes: Crafting here does not unlock Viend's shop. See Viend for trading requirements.

reports.text: Clay grants access to his alchemy workstation after the early sample quests.
After the disaster in which Commander Tain dies, Viend sets up a small alchemy workstation for the wounded.

stations.title: Armor workstation
stations.summary: Ranger Bhato's armor-crafting workstation at his hideout.
stations.acquisition: Use Ranger Bhato's workstation at his hideout after returning with the rune and completing his follow-up conversation.

stations.title: Raft Base
stations.summary: Complete a placed raft through its menu. This changes the raft in place, not into an inventory item.

merchant_profiles.conditions: Clay trades in the Fort Solid undercroft before the explosion. He survives outside afterward but no longer offers Trade, and leaves later in his conversation sequence.
Bhato's Trade option can be temporarily hidden by quest conversations.

Viend is with Clay after his escort, but starts trading only after Clay leaves, you pick up Ward Breaker, and Eir announces that Viend will handle supplies. His presence or nearby alchemy workstation alone does not unlock Trade.
Tain trades inside Fort Solid when his Trade dialogue is available. He dies in the explosion and the entrance is removed, closing the shop. This does not create a normal lootable corpse.
Reach Gurb-Gurb and use his Trade dialogue.
Complete Ihar's introductory conversation to unlock Trade.

unit_prices.context: Standard unit purchase cost: the trade menu sums final item-definition price times quantity. The original definitions either have no components or are the explicitly excluded Lamp Oil recipe. Six additional definitions retain their initializer prices after the actual numeric-ID-ordered recipe-value pass, including its comparison and rounding semantics. These are not resale values of damaged or partly burned items; separately authored vendor-specific prices remain distinct.

documented_build.confirmation: The wiki operator identified the installed game as the latest patch, 0.8.1.5, on 2026-09-25. The inspected menu code independently contains the same displayed version label; no external release-feed verification is asserted.

rules.text: One silver coin has the value of 100 copper coins. One gold coin has the value of 10 silver coins, or 1,000 copper coins.
Offer coins without buying anything, then confirm the trade. The merchant returns change in gold first, then silver, then copper.
rules.qualification: Describe descending-denomination change, not an absolute guarantee of the mathematically fewest coins at every floating-point rounding boundary. Copper change is rounded to a whole coin.

rules.text: The item's base weight is multiplied by its stack quantity. Coin weights are 25 g for copper, 30 g for silver, and 55 g for gold. Consolidating equal value into higher denominations substantially reduces carried weight.
rules.qualification: Use the coin pages as the sole editable home of the individual weights. Kilograms are corroborated by the carry-limit calculation and Pack Mule's localized kilogram-per-rank description. Ordinary coin stacks do not enter the food, special-container or equipped-armor weight adjustments.

rules.text: Shops share the same rates, with no merchant, player or difficulty markup. Purchases use full item value; resale depends on condition. Bought items have full durability and fuel. Quest items cannot be sold. Rift Weave cannot be sold until after Clay's initial sample investigation.
rules.qualification: An unchanged, full-condition item therefore has the same underlying buy and sell value. The affordability check and copper change involve rounding, so do not promise exact conservation of arbitrary sub-copper fractions.

rules.text: Listed wares do not run out, and merchants have unlimited buying funds.
rules.qualification: These rules apply to available shops, not story gifts or exchanges. Dialogue and sale restrictions still apply. Display quantities are samples, not finite stock. Summoned characters cannot be interacted with. Clay, Bhato, Tain, Viend, Gurb-Gurb and Ihar have wares; Wilda's Trade option has no wares. Wilda's normal encounter availability is unknown.

rules.text: Resale value is standard value multiplied by remaining durability as a fraction of maximum, with a 10% floor. Half durability gives half value; one-tenth durability or less gives 10%.
rules.qualification: Items without durability use full value. There is no second wear discount.

rules.text: For items with a burn duration and remaining fuel, the fuel fraction replaces the durability factor, with a 25% floor. The two discounts do not multiply.
rules.qualification: Both a burn duration and remaining fuel are required; proximity to fire is not enough.

rules.text: Affordability compares basket totals rounded to whole copper. Change is selling value minus purchase cost: whole gold first, then whole silver, then rounded copper.
rules.qualification: There is no merchant commission. Fractions of a copper can be lost or gained through rounding.

guides.title: Sharp
paragraphs: Sharp attacks add bleeding to unarmored hit points instead of removing them immediately. Bleeding stacks and takes effect at the start of the target's turn.
Remaining bleeding spreads to the next neighboring hit point in a fixed direction. Rotating the attack changes that direction. Spreading bleeding can reach beneath armor.
An initial sharp hit normally removes armor without causing bleeding on that cell. At rank 10, Blade Master lets remaining damage cause bleeding after breaking armor.
Apply an Improvised Bandage or Bandage to bleeding cells. Bandages stop bleeding but do not restore lost hit points.

guides.title: Poison
paragraphs: Poison stacks on individual hit points. At the start of the target's turn, a poisoned cell is lost and one poison counter is spent. Remaining poison can spread to a random adjacent healthy cell, including diagonals.
Spreading poison can reach beneath armor. An ordinary direct poison hit removes one armor layer instead of poisoning an armored cell. Thrown poison has different rules; see the flask's effect.
Minor Antidote and Antidote clear poison from the cells they cover without restoring lost hit points. Natural Antidote can reduce poison before it takes effect.

guides.title: Blunt
paragraphs: Blunt damage removes armor before the protected hit point. A successful blunt attack has a base 12% chance to stun a surviving target, making it lose its next turn.
Master Basher raises stun chance and reduces blunt melee AP costs at rank milestones.

guides.title: Piercing
paragraphs: Piercing damage removes armor before the protected hit point. After each point of damage, if armor or HP remains on that cell, there is a 15% chance to remove one more layer or hit point.
Multi-point hits can make several checks. Piercing does not bypass armor.

guides.title: Force
paragraphs: Force damage removes armor before the protected hit point. Each positive-damage attack cell that hits a living part of the target has a base 15% chance to deal one extra damage to an eligible neighboring cell.
The extra hit can strike diagonally and must remove armor before HP. Force Fighter raises this chance and reduces force melee AP costs at rank milestones.

guides.title: Fire
paragraphs: Ordinary direct fire attacks remove armor before burning the hit point underneath. Thrown fire has different rules; see the flask's effect. Wound salves and resting cannot restore burned cells.
Simple Burn Remedy turns a burn into an ordinary wound. It does not restore HP immediately; heal the wound afterward.

guides.title: Weak
paragraphs: Weak damage removes armor before the protected hit point. It has no extra effect: no bleeding, poison, burns, stun, piercing or force damage.

guides.title: Health and armor
paragraphs: Each occupied health-grid cell contains one HP. Empty positions cannot be hit.
Each HP cell can have up to three armor layers. Armor is not extra health.
Place an attack pattern over the target's health grid. Only overlapping cells can hit. Each number is that cell's damage range; rotation and dodging change the overlap.
The grids show starting health and armor. Wounds, story events, equipment, skills, ammunition and status effects can change combat results.
Ammunition adds bonus damage to a bow's pattern. Roll its bonus range separately for each occupied attack cell.
Wellbeing is separate from combat HP. Resting can heal ordinary wounds when its recovery conditions are met, but not burns.

guides.title: Satiation
paragraphs: Eating restores satiation. On Medium difficulty, an ordinary turn removes 0.715 percentage points before skill modifiers. Resting and sleeping reduce this loss; see Resting.
At 50% or more, satiation adds 0.5 percentage points of wellbeing per turn. From 20% to below 50% it is neutral. Below 20%, the penalty grows to 1 percentage point per turn at zero satiation.
Slow Metabolism reduces satiation loss. Skill and difficulty modifiers multiply; see Wellbeing for difficulty rates.

Eating without getting sick grants Well fed if satiation ends above 90%. Duration depends on the food's base satiation, up to 35 turns. Well fed reduces stamina loss, not wellbeing loss directly; see Stamina.
See Foods for filling meals and sickness risks. Herbivore improves satiation from foods the game treats as plant-based.
guides.image_caption: Loaf of Bread is one source of satiation.

guides.title: Stamina
paragraphs: Ending a turn restores 4 percentage points of stamina per unused AP, except while swimming or drowning. Spending all AP leaves no ordinary recovery.
At 50% or more, stamina adds 0.2 percentage points of wellbeing per turn. From 20% to below 50% it is neutral. Below 20%, the penalty grows to 0.5 percentage points per turn at zero stamina.

Stamina below 30%, 15% and 5% adds 1, 2 and 3 percentage points of accident risk, respectively: cumulative totals of 1%, 3% and 6%. This applies to actions with accident checks, not every turn. Focus and encumbrance can add more risk.
Well fed halves stamina loss. It multiplies with the difficulty rates on Wellbeing and does not reduce unused-AP recovery. See Satiation for how to gain it.

Swimming drains stamina at turn end instead of restoring it; running out can cause drowning. Beds and bedrolls have their own recovery. Normal AP replenishment pauses in bed, so do not count unused-AP recovery twice. See Resting.
Wayfarer's Vigor restores stamina over time. Bramble Berries and Bursthopper restore it immediately.
guides.image_caption: Wayfarer's Vigor grants temporary stamina recovery.

guides.title: Focus
paragraphs: On Medium difficulty, an ordinary active turn removes 0.56 percentage points of focus before skill modifiers. Resting and sleeping restore focus and reduce its loss.
At 50% or more, focus adds 0.2 percentage points of wellbeing per turn. From 20% to below 50% it is neutral. Below 20%, the penalty grows to 0.5 percentage points per turn at zero focus.

Focus below 30%, 15% and 5% adds 1, 2 and 3 percentage points of accident risk, respectively: cumulative totals of 1%, 3% and 6%. The action must have an accident check. Stamina and encumbrance can add more risk.
Focused Mind and difficulty modify focus loss, not direct gains from rest or sleep. See Wellbeing for difficulty rates.
Cranberries restore focus immediately. Sleep until rested ends at full focus; sleep until sunrise follows the sunrise schedule, not a fixed turn count.
guides.image_caption: A Tattered Bedroll provides a place to rest or sleep.

guides.title: Temperature
paragraphs: The comfortable temperature range is 40-60%. These are game-meter percentages, not degrees. There is no temperature penalty to wellbeing within that range.
Outside the comfortable range, the wellbeing penalty grows to 3 percentage points per turn at either 0% or 100% temperature. High temperature gives no bonus.

Each turn, body temperature moves one third of the way toward local ambient temperature before cooling modifiers. Insulation pulls it toward the comfortable midpoint. Wetness pulls it toward 10%, so rain and immersion can chill you even in mild air.
Body Warmth reduces cooling loss and improves drying. Difficulty also modifies cooling losses, not every temperature change; see Wellbeing.

Nearby active fires warm and dry you. Warm to the core halves ambient cooling; see Wellbeing for its other bonus. Shelter reduces rain exposure and can cool hot conditions. Equipment condition affects insulation and waterproofing; sleeping gear helps while in use.
Pleasant Vegetable Soup, Tasty Crab Soup and Survivor's Delight grant temporary warmth. Baby Firelouse does too, but also causes a fire hit.
guides.image_caption: An active nearby Campfire can warm and dry you.

guides.title: Wellbeing
paragraphs: Wellbeing is separate from combat HP. Each turn combines Satiation, Stamina, Focus and Temperature with active effects. At zero wellbeing, you die.

A percentage point changes a 0-100% meter; it is not a multiplier. Each meter's wellbeing contribution rounds to 0.1 percentage-point steps before the display settles. All meters stay between zero and 100%.
Warm to the core and Well rested each add 1 percentage point per turn. Well fed instead conserves stamina. See Temperature, Resting and Satiation for their triggers.

Sickness I, II and III remove 1, 2 and 3 percentage points per turn; only the highest active level counts. Being very overburdened removes 1 and extremely overburdened removes 2. The lighter overburdened state increases movement costs and accident risk without a direct wellbeing penalty.

Compared with Medium, Easy multiplies satiation, stamina, focus and cooling losses by 0.67; Hard multiplies them by 1.2. Skill and temporary-effect modifiers multiply with these rates. Direct recovery gains are unaffected, and cooling modifiers do not slow every temperature change.
High wellbeing does not instantly restore combat HP. See Resting for natural wound healing; burns cannot heal this way.
Honey improves wellbeing and shortens sickness. Riftvine Berries reduce wellbeing.
guides.image_caption: Honey has a direct wellbeing benefit as well as food value.

guides.title: Resting
paragraphs: Resting and sleeping restore focus and stamina, but time, weather and temperature keep advancing. See Action points for turn duration.
Ground rest adds 2 percentage points of focus per turn and halves ordinary satiation and focus losses. Unused AP restores stamina. Rest ends at full focus and stamina, or when interrupted manually.

Bed and bedroll rest gives the same focus gain and half-rate losses, plus 32 percentage points of stamina per turn. Sleep gives 2.5 focus and 32 stamina, with satiation and focus losses at 35% of normal. Normal AP replenishment pauses in bed; do not double-count stamina recovery.
Sleep until rested ends at full focus; sleep until sunrise follows the sunrise schedule. Disturbance can wake you. Below 45% wellbeing, a falling wellbeing trend can also force you awake.

Sleeping can grant Well rested above 95% focus, with satiation and stamina above 20% and temperature strictly inside its comfortable range. Sleeping-item comfort sets the duration added, up to 35 turns. The timer can pause in bed when at least two of the three supporting conditions hold. See Wellbeing for its bonus.

At 50% wellbeing or more, resting can heal one ordinary wounded combat cell. The chance depends on satiation, stamina, focus and the temperature penalty. With full supporting meters and no temperature penalty, it is 5% per resting turn. Burns cannot heal this way.

Find shelter, warmth and food before a long rest. Sleeping gear contributes insulation and waterproofing while in use. Great Bedroll and Furhide Bedroll also slow Warm to the core decay, but hunger, cold, sickness and interruptions still apply.
guides.image_caption: A Great Bedroll provides sleeping comfort and protection.

guides.title: Foods
paragraphs: Foods differ in satiation, sickness risk and other effects. See each item for stats, recipes and ways to obtain it.
Herbivore increases satiation from foods the game treats as plant-based, not all food. Satiation stops at 100%.

Eating rolls the food's sickness risk. A meal that does not cause sickness may extend Well fed; see Satiation for its trigger and Stamina for its effect. Sickness and Well fed act separately from satiation's ordinary wellbeing contribution.
Honey improves wellbeing and shortens sickness. Bramble Berries and Bursthopper restore stamina; Cranberries restore focus. Riftvine Berries reduce wellbeing. See each item for amounts.
Pleasant Vegetable Soup, Tasty Crab Soup and Survivor's Delight grant temporary warmth. Baby Firelouse also warms you but causes a fire hit.
Recipes list ingredients, outputs, AP and workstation requirements. Check the resulting food's sickness risk: preparation does not always make food safe.
guides.image_caption: Pleasant Vegetable Soup provides food and temporary warmth.

guides.title: Weather
paragraphs: Clear, cloudy and rainy weather can change when a completed turn crosses an hour boundary. Ambient temperature approaches a time-of-day target with small random variation. It is separate from body temperature.
Dry spells increase cloud and rain chances; accumulated rain encourages clearing. The ordered hourly checks are below.
On Easy and Medium, clouds cannot start new rain while fewer than two days have been survived. Hard has no early-game protection. Clouds can still form during the protected period.
Wet clothing can dampen its wearer and other carried clothing. Wetness affects body Temperature; waterproofing, shelter and drying help alongside insulation.

Lesser shelter blocks 80% of rain and stronger shelter blocks 95%. Shelter can cool hot conditions. Nearby active fires warm and dry you. Dungeon-like areas use a separate ambient temperature baseline.
Weather and temperature keep changing while you rest. Check your shelter, clothing and wellbeing trend before sleeping.
guides.image_caption: Protective clothing such as a Traveller's Cloak matters when travelling in wet weather.

guides.title: Action points
paragraphs: Attacking, equipping, crafting and applying remedies each cost AP. Costs can include fractions.
The player normally has 8 AP per turn. Spending the remaining AP ends the turn. The next turn restores AP minus any cost carried over.
Outside combat, some actions can exceed your remaining AP and carry the excess into the next turn. In combat, the required AP must be available.
Unused AP can restore stamina, with swimming and bed-rest exceptions; see Stamina. The clock advances per completed turn, not per AP.
Equipping costs a base 0.4 AP per square of inventory footprint, separate from attacking or using the item.
Fast Draw reduces bow costs; Blade Master, Master Basher and Force Fighter reduce costs for their weapon types. Brewer reduces alchemy costs.
Completed turns also update satiation, focus, temperature and wellbeing. Rest and sleep change recovery rates but do not pause these meters.

guides.title: Armor points
section_titles: From armor value to armor points
paragraphs: Every equipped item with an armor value adds it to your Total Armor, shown on the equipment screen. Clothing counts as well as armor: shirts, socks, hoods and cloaks often add a fraction of a point. All four hand slots count, so a shield on your inactive weapon set still adds its armor.

Each item adds its armor value multiplied by its current durability divided by its maximum durability, rounded to two decimals. A Steel Chestplate (6 armor, 300 durability) adds 6 when undamaged and 3 at 150 durability. Total Armor is then rounded to one decimal.

When combat begins, Total Armor is rounded down to whole armor points. Fractions are added together before rounding, so a 0.5 shirt, 0.5 pants and 0.1 socks give 1.1 Total Armor and 1 armor point. Each armor point adds one armor layer to one HP cell. A 2.9 total still gives only 2 points.
Each HP cell holds at most three armor layers. You receive at most three points for each HP cell still alive when combat begins; any Total Armor beyond that cap is not used for that fight.

You must place your armor points before combat can proceed. Left-click an HP cell to add a layer and right-click to remove one. Even clears your placement and fills cells row by row from the top left, one layer per cell on each pass. Random clears your placement and puts each point on a random cell. Done finishes placement; any points not yet placed are lost for that fight. Ending your turn is blocked until you press Done.

Equipping armor during combat gives no extra points until the next fight. Unequipping an item with an armor value during combat strips its full undamaged armor value, rounded to the nearest whole number with halves rounding up, from random armored cells. When no hostiles remain, all armor layers are removed until the next fight.
Creatures do not choose placement. Their armor is layered automatically when they appear, row by row from the top left like Even. Their health grids show the result; see Health and armor.

guides.title: Tree health and chopping
paragraphs: Every part of a tree or shrub, from trunk to twig, has its own life value between 0 and 1. The Harvest menu shows it as a freshness label: Very Fresh from about 0.88 life, Fresh from about 0.63, Half Dead from about 0.38, Mostly Dead from about 0.13 and Dead below that. A plant starts at full life, and each new branch starts with the life of the part it grows from.

No. Life never goes back up, but most trees lose almost none. Plants grow only while you are away: when you return to an outdoor area, each plant catches up about one growth step per three hours you were gone, counting at most 240 hours. On each step a part of a Willow, Cypress, Trollgnarl or Elderwort Shrub has a small chance to lose some life. The chance is negligible on low, wet ground and rises the higher the ground sits within the range where the species grows. A trunk at the top of that range loses about a third of its life over a ten-day absence on average, while a lowland tree stays fresh. Low inner branches of tall trees are far more at risk and can die off on high ground. Trees in Withered Mire and Rift-Thorn Mire decay slightly faster, Elderwort Shrubs eight times slower, and Brambles and Rift Vine never lose life this way.

A branch cannot stay much healthier than the part it grows from. On each growth step where a part's parent has lower life, the part's life moves halfway to its parent's. Once a parent falls below 0.33 life, the parts on it stop growing, so a dying trunk drags its whole crown down with it.

Rifts dry out nearby plants of every kind, including Brambles and Rift Vine. When a rift opens, and every in-game hour while it stays open in your area, each plant part within 60 pixels of a small rift or 192 pixels of a large one has a two-in-three chance to lose 0.01 to 0.1 life. That averages about 0.04 life per hour, so a fresh part beside an open rift falls below 0.33 in roughly 18 hours. Plants still catching up on growth are skipped.

A part at 0.33 life or less is dead wood: it shows no leaves and grows no new branches. This point falls inside the Mostly Dead label. Lower life also makes new branches less likely and fades a part toward pale grey. A part at 0.001 life or less becomes fully dead at 0.

Chopping a part costs action points. The cost starts at 24 times the part's size, divided by a dryness factor: the life the part has lost, rounded to the nearest tenth and counted as at least 0.1, times 5. A nearly full-life part costs 48 times its size, a half-dead part 9.6 times and a dead part 4.8 times, so dead wood is ten times cheaper to cut.

On a Willow, Cypress or Trollgnarl the trunk's cost is multiplied by 1.33 plus its size. The menu names a trunk a Branch below size 0.2, a Thick Branch below 0.3 and a Trunk otherwise; other parts are Twigs below 0.2, Branches below 0.4 and Thick Branches above. Every cost is then capped at 32 AP before the species multiplier and the tool are applied.
Willow has no species multiplier, so its hardest fresh cut costs 32 AP before the tool.
Cypress costs 1.2 times as much after the cap, up to 38.4 AP before the tool. It is common in Drowned Fen.
Trollgnarl is the hardest tree to chop: its cost is doubled after the cap, up to 64 AP before the tool. It is common in Withered Mire.

Elderwort Shrub ignores dryness and the trunk multiplier: its stem costs 8 times its size and other parts 4 times theirs. Parts below size 0.33 are Twigs and the rest Branches. It is common in Sunken Ancient Ruins.

Brambles and Rift Vine use only the basic size and dryness cost, and every part is listed as a Twig. Since they never lose life while growing, only rifts dry them out. Rift Vine is common in Rift-Thorn Mire.

The cost is divided by the chopping strength of the tool you pick, rounded to the nearest 0.2 AP, and is never below 0.2 AP. Any carried item with a chopping strength can be picked; with no tool you chop barehanded at strength 1. Felling axes are strongest, while a Serpent Fang doubles the cost. Each successful chop wears down the tool, but bare hands never wear out.

Action points are not whole numbers: a chop takes exactly the cost shown, such as 2.4 AP, and costs are shown to one decimal place. A chop is refused if it costs more than your 8 AP maximum, and a falling part cannot be chopped. Outside combat you may chop with less AP than the cost: your AP drops to 0, your turn ends and the shortfall comes out of your next turn. In combat you must have enough AP. Like any action, chopping tires you; see Stamina.

When the cut lands, the part falls with everything growing from it. With low focus or stamina, or under some effects, a swing can go wrong: the AP is spent, the part stays standing and you lose 2 wellbeing.

paragraphs: Eating Honey adds 1 percentage point of wellbeing and reduces sickness duration.
Drinking Wayfarer's Vigor adds 20 turns to a temporary effect that restores 12 percentage points of stamina each turn.
Eating Bramble Berries restores 5 percentage points of stamina.
Eating Riftvine Berries removes 5 percentage points of wellbeing.
Eating Cranberries restores 1 percentage point of focus.
Eating Pleasant Vegetable Soup adds five turns of Warm to the core.
Eating Tasty Crab Soup adds five turns of Warm to the core.
Eating Survivor's Delight adds five turns of Warm to the core.
Eating Baby Firelouse adds ten turns of Warm to the core but also causes a fire hit.
Eating Bursthopper restores 15 percentage points of stamina.

factions.title: Friendly NPC faction
factions.summary: Friendly NPCs skip the player and faction-mates during normal target acquisition. Retaliation can still target an attacker.

factions.title: Wildlife faction
factions.summary: This shared wildlife faction crosses appearance groups: flies, gnats, crabs, Mirk rodents, Mudfin, Razorfin and Mire Serpent normally exclude one another as targets.

factions.title: Giant Slug faction
factions.summary: Giant Slugs form a separate faction, not part of the mixed wildlife faction.

factions.title: Scaalmyr faction
factions.summary: Sceetler, Scaal, Scaalmyr fighters and Mutated Unwanted share this targeting faction despite their different names and appearance.

factions.title: Toadkin faction
factions.summary: Toadkin form their own targeting faction.

factions.title: Viper faction
factions.summary: Viper and Red Fang share a faction. Mire Serpent instead belongs to the mixed wildlife faction.

factions.title: Nightmare faction
factions.summary: Both Nightmare and Raving Unwanted can select other members of this same faction as targets. Neither selects itself.

factions.title: Troll faction
factions.summary: Swamp Troll and Cave Troll share this faction.

paragraphs: Beings normally avoid targeting their own faction. Nightmare and Raving Unwanted are exceptions: they can target each other, but never themselves.
Friendly NPCs also avoid targeting the player, who belongs to a separate faction.
An eligible target must still pass distance, detection, reachability and sometimes line-of-sight checks. Aggression chance and current targets also matter.
Taking damage can make a being retaliate without the usual faction check. Friendly NPCs and faction-mates can therefore fight back.
